tip: Optional. Path to a file whose contents become --template-content. Relative path only. Mutually exclusive with --template-content.

option.name: --to
tip: Optional. Default To recipient list. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.

next.name: +template-update
tip: Update an existing mail template. Supports --inspect (read-only projection), --print-patch-template (prints a JSON skeleton for --patch-file), and flat flags (--set-subject / --set-name / etc). Internally it GETs the template, applies the patch, rewrites local paths to cid: refs, and PUTs a full-replace update (no optimistic locking: last-write-wins).

option.name: --attach
tip: Additional non-inline attachment file path(s), comma-separated. Each file is uploaded to Drive and appended to the template's attachments[] in the exact flag order.

option.name: --format
tip: output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")

option.name: --inspect
tip: Inspect the template without modifying it. Returns the current template projection (name/subject/addresses/attachments). No write is performed.

option.name: --jq
tip: jq expression to filter JSON output

option.name: --mailbox
tip: Mailbox email address that owns the template (default: me).

option.name: --patch-file
tip: Path to a JSON patch file (relative path only). Shape is the same as --print-patch-template output.

option.name: --print-patch-template
tip: Print a JSON template describing the supported --patch-file structure. No network call is made.

option.name: --set-bcc
tip: Replace the Bcc recipient list. Pass --set-bcc="" to clear the list.

option.name: --set-cc
tip: Replace the Cc recipient list. Pass --set-cc="" to clear the list.

option.name: --set-template-content
tip: Replace the template body content. Prefer HTML for rich formatting.

option.name: --set-template-content-file
tip: Replace template body content with the contents of a file (relative path only). Mutually exclusive with --set-template-content.

option.name: --set-to
tip: Replace the To recipient list. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Pass --set-to="" to clear the list.

option.name: --template-id
tip: Template ID to update. Required except when using --print-patch-template by itself.

next.name: +thread
tip: Use when querying a full mail conversation/thread by thread ID. Returns all messages in chronological order, including replies and drafts, with body content and attachments metadata, including inline images.

option.name: --format
tip: output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")

option.name: --html
tip: Whether to return HTML body (false returns plain text only to save bandwidth) (default true)

option.name: --include-spam-trash
tip: Also return messages from SPAM and TRASH folders (excluded by default)

option.name: --jq
tip: jq expression to filter JSON output

option.name: --print-output-schema

next.name: +triage

option.name: --filter

option.name: --folder

option.name: --format
tip: output format: table | json | data (json/data output object with pagination fields) (table|json|data) (default "table")

option.name: --jq
tip: jq expression to filter JSON output

option.name: --max
tip: maximum number of messages to fetch (1-400; auto-paginates internally) (default 20)

option.name: --page-token
tip: pagination token from a previous response to fetch the next page

option.name: --query
tip: full-text keyword search across from/to/subject/body (max 50 chars). Example: "budget report"

next.name: +watch

option.name: --folder-ids

option.name: --folders

option.name: --format
tip: json: NDJSON stream with ok/data envelope; data: bare NDJSON stream (json|data) (default "data")

option.name: --jq
tip: jq expression to filter JSON output

option.name: --label-ids
tip: filter: label IDs JSON array, e.g. ["FLAGGED","IMPORTANT"]

option.name: --labels

option.name: --msg-format
tip: message payload mode: metadata(headers + meta, for triage/notification) | minimal(IDs and state only, no headers, for tracking read/folder changes) | plain_text_full(all metadata fields + full plain-text body) | event(raw WebSocket event, no API call, for debug) | full(full message including HTML body and attachments) (default "metadata")

option.name: --output-dir
tip: Write each message as a JSON file (always full payload, regardless of --msg-format)

option.name: --print-output-schema
tip: Print output field reference per --msg-format (run this first to learn field names before parsing output)

option.name: --styles
tip: {styles:[...]} Visual spec JSON applied to an EXISTING spreadsheet: top-level {styles:[...]}, one item per target sheet (`name` is the real sheet name), each giving at least one of `cell_styles` / `cell_merges` / `row_sizes` / `col_sizes` / `freeze`. option.name: --max-chars
tip: Max output chars per call; default 500000 (safety cap). The underlying tool truncates at ~50000 even when unset, so this is sent explicitly to raise it; for a full untruncated read use --output-path (cap auto-raises to a bounded 20M chars; explicit --max-chars overrides). Passing 0 means "no cap of my own" and resolves to the same ceiling as leaving the flag alone (500000, or the offload limit with --output-path) — never down to the tool's smaller omitted-value fallback. (default 500000)

option.name: --output-path
tip: ./out.json Write the full read result to a local path (e.g. ./out.json); the file holds the data payload as JSON while stdout returns only a small confirmation (output_path, byte count). **When set, the char cap auto-raises to a bounded offload default (20M chars)** rather than unlimited — the read path is not streaming, so this cap is the memory guard; an explicit --max-chars overrides it. The stdout receipt reports `complete` (and `truncated` plus a warning when the cap was hit), so check it instead of assuming the file holds the whole sheet. Omit it to print to stdout as usual.

option.name: --sheets
tip: {"sheets":[...]} Typed table payload (pandas-DataFrame-shaped) as JSON: top-level {"sheets":[...]}, with each array item a sub-sheet `{name, start_cell?, mode?, header?, allow_overwrite?, columns:["colA","colB",...], data:[[...]], dtypes?:{colA:pandasDtype, ...}, formats?:{colA:numberFormat, ...}}` — `name` and the outer `sheets` envelope are both required. Agents typically use `df_to_sheet(df, name)` from `scripts/sheets_df.py` to pack each DataFrame into one item, then wrap the list in `{"sheets":[...]}`. `dtypes` values are pandas dtype strings (`int64`, `float64`, `Int64`, `bool`, `boolean`, `datetime64[ns]`, `object`, ...); the writer maps them to internal string/number/date/bool — omit `dtypes` and a column writes as text (good for raw CSV-shaped data). `formats[col]` is an Excel number_format string (e.g. `#,##0.00`, `0.0%`, `yyyy-mm`); when absent, date columns default to `yyyy-mm-dd` and string columns to text format (`@`).
